label: text
text: Berlin, July 1.

label: text
text: The Ukrainian Government is negotiating with the Rhein Metall one of Germany's biggest machinery works, for the sale of the latter's entire locomotive department. The Russians propose to regret the works at Kharkoff and take over the German staff for the purpose of building engines for the Russian railways.

label: text
text: The purchase price is sold to be about £6,000,000.—Rent.

label: paragraph_title
text: PLOT FAILS.

label: text
text: KING ALFONSO IN DANGER IN PARIS.

label: text
text: Paris, July 1.

label: text
text: Following their departure for London of the King and Queen of Spain on a fortnight's private visit, the police have revealed a plot to assassinate the King which was frustrated on Friday by the arrest of two notorious bandits and inarchists who had come purposely from Argentine.

label: text
text: One is said to be the murderer of the Archbishop of Saragossa in 1923. They confessed that they intended to made an attempt on the King's life.

label: text
text: The police have been watching five individuals who landed at Cherbourg from the Argentine at the beginning of May. Two Spaniards, Ascasa, suspected of the Saragossa murder, and Bonaventur Adurety, using false names, were arrested at a family pension. They were armed with automatics, and Ascasa attempted to fire on the police, but was overpowered. A thousand pesos bank-note payable on the Italian Bank, a receipt for a motor-car purchase, three rifles and 240 cartridges were discovered in the rooms of Ascasa, who said he intended to motor to the last station outside Paris where the Royal train would stop and where an attempt would have been made.

label: text
text: L'Oeuvre publishes a messed from Hendaye that as a result of the plot, the Spanish Government have arrested over four hundred militarists. The prisons are crowded with civilians, including Melquiado Alvarez, the ex-Premier.

label: text
text: Count Romanones, threatened with arrest, has fled from Hendaye. Reuter.

label: text
text: Visit to Buckingham.

label: text
text: The King and Queen of Spain who are staying at Claridge's Hotel, were visited this morning by the Prince of Wales, the Duke and Duchess of York, and other royalties.

label: text
text: Afterward King Alfonso and Queen Ena left for Buckingham Palace, where they lunched with King George and Queen Mary.

label: text
text: In the afternoon their Spanish Majesties drove to Wimbledon lawn tennis tournament to see.Senorita de Alvarez play in the semi-final match in the women's singles. British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: WEMBLEY.

label: paragraph_title
text: BEST OFFER FOR THE SITE ACCEPTED.

label: text
text: The liquidators of the British Empire Exhibition announce that Wembley was sold to the Beecham Trust and James White for £300,000 which in view of the fact that the liquidators are also indemnified against certain liabilities and expenses, is the best offer received. A further call on the guarantees is necessary. —Router.

label: paragraph_title
text: DOUBLE EDGE

label: text
text: CANTON LABOUR UNIONS POSITION.

label: text
text: VOLUNTEERS WANTED

label: text
text: Canton's labour unions are now being called upon to provide transport coolies for the military. When the wave of "national feeling" was at its highest, the labour organisations were given all kinds of power. The other edge of the knife is now making itself felt. According to vernacular reports, each union will have to enroll a fixed number of volunteers for the Northern front, failure to which will mean that the offending unions will have their charters revoked. The reports also indicate that this order has not been favourably received by the representatives of patriotic workers.

label: paragraph_title
text: AND STRIKERS' TOOL

label: text
text: [From Our Own Correspondent.]

label: text
text: Because of the shortage of coolies for the military expedition, and failure in recruiting volunteers, the Military Council has put upon the "Hongkong Canton Strike Committee" the duty of furnishing all coolies needed. Six hundred strikers were sent to Shukwan a fortnight ago, and yesterday 500 more embarked but at least 1,500 more are needed at once, and these the strikers will have to find.

label: paragraph_title
text: ABERDEEN FATALITY.

label: text
text: The master of a shop in the Aberdeen district was drowned yesterday by the sinking of a sampun in which he was travelling with an employee.

label: text
text: In his report to the police, the employee stated that the sampan overturned when ten yards from the eastern end of Applichau island. He swam ashore, but his master was not seen.

label: text
text: An earlier search by the police having proved fruitless, the body was found beside the sunken boat after the tide had gone down.

label: text
text: A Chinese was stated to have held another man by the neck in stealing gold coins to the value of $82. The arrest of the defendant after a chase was mentioned before the Magistrate when he was sent to prison for three months.

label: text

label: text
text: Captain A. McKinnon (master of the Steamboat Co.'s "Kinshan") and Captain M. McCarthy (master of the "Paul Beau") were each fined $25 at the Marine Court this morning, on pleading guilty to charges of not having the regulation lights at 3 a.m. on June 25, when the bowls were alongside their respective wharves on the Praya.

label: text
text: The prosecutions were taken out by Lee-Sgt. Hurley.

label: text
text: Captain K. Kagikawn also "admitted the failure to exhibit lights on board the s.s. Toyo Maru No. 1 on June 29, at harbour buoy. No. 45. He was fined $25,

label: text
text: For failing to observe the rule of the road, the master of the 3.1 Yan Hing was fined $5. With two previous convictions, the master of the 3.1. Tung Sang was fined $25.

label: text
text: For going alongside the “Andre Lebon” when two other lunches were already in position, the s.1. “Kwong Chee” was fined $5, and the motor-boat “Walla—Walla—7” was fined $15 for being without lights while under way.

label: text
text: The mistress of a passenger bout was fined $3 for carrying fish and vegetables.

label: text
text: Because her dinghy was so small that it did not come within the Ordinance, the mistress of another boat was found not guilty on a charge of being without lights. This class of boat does not require both head and aft lights.

label: text
text: REFUSED TO JOIN IN ANTI-CHRISTIAN RAID.

label: text
text: Changteh, Hu.. Junê.

label: text
text: The anti-red action of the Changsha officials hindered many of the Hunan students attending the provincial athletic meeting, that held the attention of this city for three days. The courtesy of those in charge and indeed the general bearing of the students was decidedly friendly.

label: text
text: We have been expecting an invasion from the west by Long and his bandit brigade, and now that Gen. Ho has slipped away with his troops, Long's men may arrive any day. It is said that Gen. Ho got $2,000,000 for travelling expenses. He has gone to Tsengchih.—"N.C. Daily News."

label: text
text: We have enjoyed a time of comparative quiet in this city and district.

label: text
text: The fracus at the Normal School doubtless helped to this end. The Bolshevist-minded students demanded that the Kuomintang students should join them in active opposition to the churches and all British folks and goods. On the latter refusing to do so, they were attacked by their Red brethren, who stabbed and clubbed quite a number, several dying from the wounds. Then the Red leaders were arrested and their followers fled and this served to keep peace, as the officials showed a strong hand in the matter. It was greatly owing to this that the observance of the May 30 and June 1 anniversary passed off very
